context:
Accessibility work is most reliably driven by the tests themselves.
Add axe-core first, watch the existing tests fail, then fix
violations in priority order (keyboard → aria-label → contrast →
focus visibility).

For the reduced-color mode: do not build a separate component tree.
Flip a CSS class on the grid root; cell colors read from CSS custom
properties that switch value based on the class. This keeps the
render path single and the switch cost zero.

Keyboard nav is the trickiest part. Use a roving tabindex pattern
(only one cell has tabindex=0 at a time; arrow keys move it).
Reference pattern: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices grid pattern.
description:
The 2026-04-15 review flagged that the matrix leaderboard relies heavily
on color to convey information - a known accessibility hazard. Color is
invisible to screen readers and insufficient for users with color vision
deficiencies. The heatmap must remain readable without color.

This TODO:

1. Ensures each heat cell carries a descriptive `aria-label` with the
   numeric timing and the relative ratio ("18ms, 1.6× fastest").

2. Adds a "reduced color" visual mode that falls back to monochrome
   lightness steps, controlled by the user's
   `prefers-contrast: more` media query and an explicit toggle.

3. Adds keyboard navigation: tab reaches platform checkboxes,
   arrow keys navigate cells with an `aria-live` announcement.

4. Backfills snapshot tests for the filter bar, empty states, and the
   integration between BenchmarkIndex and QueryHeatmap - the prior TODO
   only specified QueryHeatmap itself.

5. Runs axe-core against the rendered matrix in the test suite and
   fails the build on any serious or critical violations.

anti_patterns.dont: duplicate the component for high-contrast mode
anti_patterns.instead: use CSS custom properties that switch on a class
anti_patterns.why: two components drift out of sync

anti_patterns.dont: fail the build on minor axe violations
anti_patterns.why: minor issues include color-contrast edge cases we may accept

anti_patterns.instead: include text and aria-label on every data-bearing element
anti_patterns.why: 4% of users have color vision deficiencies and screen readers ignore color entirely

anti_patterns.instead: use roving tabindex so tab exits the grid quickly
anti_patterns.why: that makes keyboard nav painful (tab through 22×8 cells)

preserves.behavior: Current default color mode - high-contrast is an opt-in, not a default swap
Existing behavior of the matrix - accessibility is additive layering, not a rewrite
Snapshot tests from explorer-matrix-leaderboard-view - this TODO extends, does not replace them

verifications.description: axe-core runs clean on the matrix page (no serious/critical violations)
Heat cells have aria-label with numeric content
Reduced-color mode is CSS-class driven, not a separate component

work_units.notes:
Cell: aria-label='${ms}ms, ${ratio}× fastest in column' (or
'no data' for null cells). Column headers: aria-sort='none'.
Row checkboxes: aria-label='Select ${platform} for comparison'.
work_units.summary: Enhance QueryHeatmap cells, headers, and checkboxes with descriptive aria labels

work_units.notes:
Activates when prefers-contrast: more matches OR the user toggles
'High contrast' in the filter bar. Cells use grayscale lightness
(0-100%) instead of hsl hue. Numeric text remains primary signal.
work_units.summary: Implement reduced-color mode via CSS class + custom properties

work_units.notes:
Arrow keys within the matrix move focus between cells; focused
cell announces itself via aria-live. Tab exits the grid to the
next filter control. Focus outline is visible (not just color).
work_units.summary: Add keyboard navigation (roving tabindex) and visible focus outlines

work_units.notes:
Add helper `expectNoAxeViolations(container)` and call it in
QueryHeatmap, BenchmarkIndex, Compare, and Home page tests.
Warn on minor; fail only on serious/critical.
work_units.summary: Integrate axe-core into the test suite; fail on serious/critical violations
